questions.question: A train covers a distance of 35 km in 60 min. How long will it take to cover 105 km?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered by the train = 35 km.

Time taken to cover 35 km = 60 min.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

First, find the speed of the train:

Speed = Distance / Time

Speed = 35 km / 60 min

Speed = 35 km / 1 hr

Speed = 35 km/hr

Now, find the time to cover 105 km:

Time = Distance / Speed

Time = 105 km / 35 km/hr

⇒ Time = 3 hr

Convert hours to minutes:

⇒ Time = 3 hr × 60 min/hr

⇒ Time = 180 min

**The correct answer is option 3 (180 min).**

questions.question: What is the SI unit of radioactivity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Becquerel**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **SI unit of radioactivity** is the **Becquerel (Bq)**.
 
• It measures the rate of radioactive decay, defined as one disintegration (decay) per second.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Faraday**:
 
• Named after Michael Faraday, the Faraday is a unit associated with electric charge, not radioactivity. Specifically, it refers to the charge of one mole of electrons (approximately 96,485 coulombs) and is often used in electrochemistry.
 
• **Rutherford**:
 
• The Rutherford (Rd) is an older, non-SI unit of radioactivity. It was defined as **1 million disintegrations per second** but has largely been replaced by the Becquerel in modern scientific contexts.
 
• **Curie (Ci)**:
 
• The **Curie** is another unit of radioactivity, named after Marie Curie, and was historically used before the Becquerel. One Curie equals **3.7 × 10¹⁰ disintegrations per second** (the approximate activity of 1 gram of radium-226).
 
 
• Although still sometimes used, the Curie has mostly been replaced by the Becquerel in the SI system.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a 'fundamental right' in the Indian Constitution?

__
 
• In the Indian Constitution, the right to speech is part of the Right to Freedom of Speech and Expression, which is a fundamental right under Article 19.
 
• However, the term "Right to Speech" alone is not listed as a fundamental right. 
 
• It is framed under the broader concept of **freedom of speech and expression**.
 
• This right is one of the fundamental rights but is subject to limitations, such as:
 
 
• **Security of the State**
 
• **Public Order**
 
• **Decency or Morality**
 
• **Contempt of Court**
 
• **Defamation**
 
• **Incitement to an offence**
 
 
 
• So, while "Right to Speech" is essentially covered under **Article 19(1)(a)**, it is not listed as "Right to Speech" by name in the Constitution.

questions.question: The ratio of simple interest earned by a certain amount at the rate of 5% for 6 years and 8% for 3 years is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rate of interest for the first period (R₁) = 5%

Time for the first period (T₁) = 6 years

Rate of interest for the second period (R₂) = 8%

Time for the second period (T₂) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

Ratio = SI₁ / SI₂

**Calculation:**

Let the principal amount be P.

SI₁ = (P × R₁ × T₁) / 100

SI₂ = (P × R₂ × T₂) / 100

⇒ SI₁ = (P × 5 × 6) / 100 = 30P / 100

⇒ SI₂ = (P × 8 × 3) / 100 = 24P / 100

Ratio = (30P / 100) / (24P / 100)

⇒ Ratio = 30 / 24

⇒ Ratio = 5 / 4

**The ratio of simple interest earned is 5 ∶ 4.**

Height (h) = 14 cm.

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 660 cm².

**Formula Used:**

1. Curved Surface Area of a Cylinder = 2 π r h

2. Volume of a Cylinder = π r² h

**Calculation:**

Using the CSA formula:

{CSA} = 2 pi r h

660 = 2 × (22/7) × r × 14

⇒ 330 = (22/7) × r × 14

⇒ r = 330/(2 × 22)

⇒ r = 30 / 4

⇒ r = 15/2 cm

{Volume} = pi r² h

Volume = (22/7) × (15/2)² × 14

⇒ Volume = (11/7) × 15 × 15 × 7

⇒ Volume = 11 × 15 × 15

⇒ Volume = 2475 cm³

**The volume of the cylinder is 2475 cm³.**
